purpose_of_this_fixture: Tests restraint on a thin, 12-minute intro call. A membership coordinator is 'just exploring options' for an executive director who is not on the call. She describes only a vague 'all over the place' disorganization, gives no numbers, has no view of the decision process, offers a secondhand and hedged why-now, mentions that a board member uses association software elsewhere, and doubts the society needs 'a whole system'. The Consultant adds that a better spreadsheet may be enough, and books a 45-minute discovery call for Tuesday the 22nd. Expected verdict: Not ready. R2 (no excavated pain), R4 (no cost inputs at all) and R7 (no decision process) are Missing, and R3 is only Partial. R4 alone forces Not ready, so a grader who reads R2 or R7 as Partial reaches the same verdict. Blueprint gate not met (R2 is not Met). Pricing or proposal gate not met (R4, R7 and R12 are Missing). The plugin must not propose a blueprint or build and must not invent bleed or upside figures from hedged volumes or idioms. It should produce discovery prep for the call booked for Tuesday the 22nd with at most five gap questions, core criteria first, ideally aimed at the executive director. expected_questions_before_building is the full pool in priority order, not a list to ask in one meeting.

traps: Mentions of 'the board', 'board retreat' and 'board members' mean the board of directors, not a monday board. Do not create boards from these mentions.
'or it might have been monday actually' is unconfirmed, and in lowercase captions it could read as the weekday. Ask whether an old monday account exists before assuming a new or existing account.
The membership database's name is [inaudible]. Its capabilities, export options and contract end ('next year? maybe') are unknown, and it may remain the member system of record.
Member count ('a couple thousand members? don't quote me on that') and staff count ('fifteen-ish') are hedged. Do not use them as volumes or cost inputs.
'instead of asking five people' is a figure of speech, not a headcount or cost input.
Neither the April annual conference nor 'renewal season' is a stated deadline for this project, and the timing of renewal season is never given.
Everything about Denise (what prompted this, her desired outcome, budget, the decision) is secondhand or guessed by Jolene. Do not record it as Denise's own statement.
Denise's attendance on the 22nd is unconfirmed ('she might only be able to do half'). Prep should work with or without her.

Product fit is unclear: a dedicated association management system, or 'a better spreadsheet and a couple of habits', may fit better, and the Consultant said so on the call. Do not propose a blueprint or build.
The renewal tracker contains personal data and may never arrive. Only a blank copy with headers was requested; never use member details for seed data.
One committee has two names (education / professional development), and the young professionals committee may no longer exist.

'Speaker 3' is identified as Wendell only by Jolene's next turn. He interrupts for a few seconds about another meeting and says nothing about the project; do not attribute views or a decision role to him.
The transcript carries no call date, so the month of 'tuesday the twenty second' has to come from the file's metadata or the Consultant, not a guess.
No price or rate was given ('pricing honestly depends on what we find'). Do not generate pricing or a proposal.
Denise is not a confirmed approver: Jolene does not know whether spend goes to the board. Record the approver as unknown rather than defaulting to the executive director.
'i follow up with some of them' suggests not every lapsed member gets a follow-up, but no pain, count or lost-dues figure was stated. Ask about it; do not assume a revenue leak.
'somebody set something up and then nobody used it' is an adoption warning from an earlier attempt, not a stated pain. Carry it as an anticipated objection and ask what happened.

The Consultant did ask about the decision, timing, blockers and time spent, and every answer was hedged or 'ask denise'. These are asked-but-unanswered gaps. Next prep should redirect them to Denise or reframe them, not repeat them to Jolene word for word.

'some weeks it's most of what i do and some weeks it's barely anything' is not an hours figure. Do not turn 'most of what i do' into a share of a salary or any bleed estimate; she only agreed to try to get a rough idea before the next call.
expected_questions_before_building: (R2 / P1 Concrete) When did something last slip through the cracks, whether a renewal, an event or a committee task? What happened, and who noticed?
(R2 / P1 Workaround) What do you do today to keep on top of it, and what stops you carrying on that way?
(R3, for Denise) What has made this matter now rather than last year? Did it come from the board retreat, and does the portal contract end soon (when)?

(R4) Across renewals, events and committees, roughly how many hours a week go into chasing, re-entering or reconciling information? Does every lapsed member get a follow-up, and if not, roughly how many drop away in a year?
(R7) Who else has a say, who approves spending, does it go to the board, and what happens after a yes?
(R1) Walk through one renewal end to end: portal reminder, tracker, lapsed status, follow-up, the bookkeeper's payment check, CE credits. Who touches each step, and for how long?
(R1 / adoption) Does the society already have a monday account from the conference committee's earlier attempt? Who set it up, what is in it, and why did people stop using it?
(R6, for Denise) If this were running well, what would a normal week look like, and what would the board count as a win?
(R8) Is this for this quarter or later? Is there a real deadline, such as renewal season, the April conference or the end of the portal contract?
(R9 / alternatives) Is Denise also looking at association management software? What would make the choice clear?
(Fit) Would the portal stay as the member record, and can it export or connect to other tools?
(Access and data) Would volunteer committee chairs need access, and which member data (addresses, license numbers, credits) may be stored in a new tool?
